mandatoryCriteria: FND-01: Pinned Node/Worker entry points and local PostgreSQL query/rollback run reproducibly; no cloud account required.
FND-02: Validated request/response schemas and generated OpenAPI agree; fixtures include two projects with distinct members.
FND-03: Clean install and upgrade enforce workspace/project ancestry, versions, uniqueness and receipt/outbox relationships.
FND-04: Request IDs, safe errors, deadlines, rate/body limits and structured timing work without exposing secrets.

Mounted operations enforce current identity, role/target authority, project and board grants, resource ancestry, lifecycle and receipt replay boundaries; negative cases cannot expose data or write effects.
Applicable writes preserve state/version, minimal receipt, activity and outbox atomically; real separate-connection tests cover the feature races and retention limits.

Every listed backend feature requires a fresh independent review of its complete reachable frozen source, fixed weights/category minima, unrounded score strictly greater than8.5, no blocker and actual passing checks. Builders cannot approve their own work.

Required UI and integration phases need actual test/browser evidence with current backend/UI hash bindings; source or API tests alone cannot prove UI or real-provider/hosted acceptance. Do not relabel missing mandatory behavior deferred to close a feature.
ACC-01: Chosen OAuth login creates one identity/session; unsupported callbacks fail closed and private data needs a valid session.
ACC-02: Logout revokes server session; expired tabs retain safe drafts but cannot keep reading or writing protected data.
ACC-03: Name/avatar updates display correctly; historical actors remain attributable after grant removal without leaking private account fields.

ACC-04: First authenticated use ensures one personal workspace and sole owner atomically; concurrent retries cannot create duplicates. Manual workspace creation stays retired with typed 410; project creation uses the ensured owner context.
ACC-05: Owner sets workspace name/timezone; date-only deadlines retain their selected day and shared overdue semantics.
ACC-06: Show only owned projects and explicitly granted projects; current context is reauthorized and being owner elsewhere grants no extra rights.

ACC-07: Ownership transfer stays unavailable in the current beta through every route and UI affordance; direct requests return the documented typed retirement response with no ownership/quota mutation. No transfer capability is claimed.
PRJ-01: Owner creates named projects inside their workspace; each has independent membership and boards.
PRJ-02: Owned projects and invited projects are paginated and scoped; hidden projects leak no name, count or existence.
PRJ-03: Owner/manager updates project name/description using expected version; managers cannot alter workspace ownership.
PRJ-04: Owner archives project as read-only and can reopen; data/history remain, trash deadlines continue and new imports/writes stop.

PRJ-05: Only Owner/Project Manager can read the full project People directory including emails; Member/Viewer direct requests expose no directory data. Authorized board-scoped assignee/mention pickers remain available with eligible identities only and no unrelated-project enumeration.
INV-01: Owner invites manager/member/viewer; manager invites member/viewer only. Invitation grants only exact project membership, never implicit board access; independent board grants are explained.
INV-02: Durable invite delivery uses a configured email adapter; failure is visible and retryable without logging the secret link.
INV-03: Signed-in verified email must match unexpired, hashed, single-use project token; wrong email grants nothing.
INV-04: Authorized resend rotates token; revoke invalidates it; races create at most one grant and invitation outcome.
INV-05: Owner sees all own projects; manager sees own project invitations; expired/accepted/revoked states and next actions are clear.
INV-06: Owner appoints/removes managers; manager changes member/viewer roles only and cannot promote self or a peer manager.
INV-07: Owner removes any grant; manager removes member/viewer in own project; next API/file/import/replay access fails after revocation.
INV-08: Invitee can leave their own grant with confirmation; owner cannot leave ownership and historical authorship remains.
RBAC-01: Every endpoint derives active ownership/project grant from session; manager authority is project-scoped and member/viewer cannot administer.
RBAC-02: Guessing sibling board/card/comment/file/import IDs returns a consistent private not-found response with no metadata leakage.
RBAC-03: Grant/owner lock protocol serializes a write against role removal; no write commits after a preceding revocation wins.
RBAC-04: Search, people, assignees, mentions, inbox and historical identity responses expose only the actor's authorized project context.

RBAC-05: Membership and board access are distinct: non-Owners require both; invitations grant no boards automatically. Owner administers board grants; Manager receives creator access to a board they create. UI and APIs disclose current effective access without hidden-board metadata.
BRD-01: Owner/manager creates a board with default columns atomically inside an authorized project.

BRD-02: List only currently accessible project boards; Owner alone edits board name/description with expected version without breaking card IDs/links. Metadata-only machine credentials receive only their explicitly allowed fields.
BRD-03: Metadata, counts and first column pages share one snapshot; caps/cursors are explicit and all filters count beyond the visible page.
BRD-04: Owner/manager configures unique normalized names, colors and todo/active/done categories with expected board version.
BRD-05: Pointer and click/tap/keyboard ordering persist atomically; missing/duplicate/foreign IDs and stale revisions fail clearly.
BRD-06: Owner/manager cannot remove final column or any column referenced by active/restorable cards; no silent card deletion/move occurs.
BRD-07: Load more retains canonical order without duplicates; empty column and empty filtered column are distinct and stale cursors refresh.
BRD-08: Owner/manager makes board read-only or reopens it; no card is deleted and pending trash deadlines continue.
CRD-01: Member/manager/owner creates title in an active authorized column; required field and retry failures retain draft and create once.
CRD-02: Show title, priority, due date, assignees and accurate comment/image counts without loading full descriptions/history.
CRD-03: Card link loads an authorized popup/drawer or direct-page view with focus restoration and recoverable missing/loading states.
CRD-04: Explicit Save validates plain text and expected card version; Cancel/discard never overwrites saved state.
CRD-05: Five priority values and optional date-only deadline save/reset consistently; invalid calendar dates fail and overdue excludes done cards.
CRD-06: Assign zero/multiple active eligible project users or owner; removed identities stay labeled historical and cannot be newly assigned.
CRD-07: Server validates neighbors and versions, changes rank/history atomically and returns canonical position; failure restores server order.
CRD-08: Visible Move chooses column plus first/last/before/after via bounded placement read; equivalent outcome without dragging.
CRD-09: Explain disabled ambiguous drag while filters apply; Move uses full destination order rather than renumbering visible cards only.
CRD-10: Stale field/order version returns 409 without partial side effects; preserve draft and allow deliberate refresh/reapply.
CRD-11: Save affects fields only; comment/upload actions are independent; retries keep command identity and closing protects unsaved work.
CRD-12: Undo is a new authorized versioned move; it succeeds once or explains conflict without overwriting intervening work.
COM-01: Project readers see chronological comments with author displays; stable cursors do not expose other project content.
COM-02: Member/manager/owner posts plain text independently of card Save; atomic event/outbox/receipt and lost-response retry create one comment.
COM-03: Accessible picker resolves active project identities; validated UTF-16 spans produce mentions and literal at-name text does not notify.
COM-04: Author updates with expected version; edit activity persists and v1 edits do not resend mention notifications.
COM-05: Author or owner/manager tombstones a comment, records action and hides body from normal reads; other members cannot moderate.
COM-06: Typing, mention selection and post error survive field saves/refetch; no comment posts accidentally through Enter in a picker.
ATT-01: Authorized editor requests bounded upload and sees progress/cancel; private staging cannot attach files across projects.
ATT-02: Accept validated PNG/JPEG/WebP bytes with size/dimension/count caps; reject SVG/HTML/spoofed MIME and finalize only after verification.
ATT-03: Finalized images show filename/size/thumbnail and preview; failed or pending upload is not shown as a saved attachment.
ATT-04: Authenticated proxy checks current project access on every fetch; no public bucket/long-lived URL or project-revocation bypass.
ATT-05: Uploader or owner/manager removes image with confirmation/history; removed images are absent from active card and cleanup is retryable.
ATT-06: Expired uploads/unreferenced objects are cleaned safely; quotas fail visibly without breaking existing saved card fields.
ATT-07: Trashing card preserves finalized files until restore cutoff; restore recovers them and purge never destroys a successfully restored card's images.
DEL-01: Owner/manager confirms Delete, moves card to trash with server deletedAt/restoreUntil and immediately excludes it from active counts/search.
DEL-02: Owner/manager lists trashed cards with actor/deadline and restore action; member/viewer cannot browse trash.
DEL-03: Owner/manager restores same ID/content/comments/finalized images strictly before server cutoff; no-op repeats do not extend deadline.
DEL-04: Original valid column/nearest surviving position is default; absent/read-only destination requires explicit authorized active target or reopening board.
DEL-05: At or after deletedAt plus exactly 24 hours restore returns stable expired response even if cleanup has not run.
DEL-06: Conditional state/version and job fencing allow one winner; cleanup cannot purge restored data or files.
DEL-07: After cutoff remove recoverable content/files via retryable cleanup; retain minimal audit/duplicate tombstones with no deleted body.
DEL-08: Trashed/expired cards reject edits/moves/comments/new uploads; UI explains disappearance while retaining safe unsent drafts.
AUD-01: Owner sees create, field change, assignment, move, comment and actor/server timestamp chronologically with stable pagination.
AUD-02: Record safe before/after field values and from/to columns; historical name changes and removed people remain understandable.
AUD-03: Owner filters owned workspace activity by project/card/actor/action/date; invited users cannot access sibling-project audit data.
AUD-04: Manager sees project activity/access changes; member/viewer sees card activity only for granted project; workspace security log is owner-only.
AUD-05: Trash/restore/purge/import/image events are traceable; no secret token or raw file appears in audit payloads.
AUD-06: No user edits audit facts; sensitive/deleted bodies are redacted under retention rules while actor/action/time facts persist.
NTF-01: One event/recipient notification appears after commit; no self-mention or duplicate logical delivery and no stale private preview leak.
NTF-02: Actor opens accessible project/card and marks read; removed-access notifications are redacted/hidden and never reveal content.
NTF-03: Lease/fenced consumer retries bounded jobs and quarantines failures; restart/duplicate handling does not lose accepted notification intent.
QRY-01: Title search returns authorized active cards only with pagination and safe historical people mapping.
QRY-02: Filters combine predictably, distinguish total/matching counts and exclude trash; no global project discovery through query parameters.
QRY-03: Show actor assignments within one selected authorized project and currently granted boards with due-state filters/pagination; no cross-project aggregation or revoked-access content.
UX-01: First project/empty board/no matches/loading/offline/validation/permission errors have accurate actions and preserve relevant drafts.
UX-02: Keyboard and click/tap complete all essential operations; focus, announcements, labels and color-independent cues are verified in browser.
UX-03: Board scroll and detail layout work at narrow width/zoom; long titles, many assignees and image/comment lists remain usable.
UX-04: Pause hidden-tab polling, refresh on focus and reconcile versions; no optimistic duplicate/older response overwrites newer data.
UX-05: Representative Worker/Node warm/cold benchmarks, project isolation, exact restore boundary and repeated import pass documented gates.
IMP-01: Versioned seven-column Cards template plus Instructions downloads without example rows in the import sheet.
IMP-02: Owner/manager chooses one project/board and default column; upload cannot create projects/users/grants or override destination.
IMP-03: Accept supported XLSX only, enforce compressed/expanded/cell/row limits and reject formulas/macros/external package links without evaluating them.
IMP-04: Exact seven headers map shared card validators; status/date/email errors name row/field and no invalid value is silently guessed.
IMP-05: Preview counts new/already-imported/conflicting/invalid rows, displays mapping and writes no cards; user corrects errors before confirming.
IMP-06: Bind preview to actor/target/digest/expiry; revalidate grant/columns/assignees and create all new rows in one bounded transaction or none.
IMP-07: Board-scoped text External ID preserves zeros; duplicate upload/race creates once, changed ID payload conflicts and deleted imports never resurrect silently.
IMP-08: Real 1900/1904 Excel dates or strict ISO map to date-only values; semicolon emails resolve active eligible project users only.
IMP-09: Result links created cards and row outcomes; safe report cannot execute spreadsheet formulas or leak another project's data.
IMP-10: Cancel before commit/expiry cleans temporary content; once transaction begins show actual final result rather than promise cancellation.
IMP-11: Import receipt links actor/batch/rows/created cards, while each card behaves like a normal card with a creation activity event.
OAUTH-01 Explicit canonical APP_ORIGIN determines issuer/resource; only an explicit NODE_ENV=test loopback override allows HTTP/ports.
OAUTH-02 Bounded CIMD fetch only from strict HTTPS claude.ai non-root URLs; no credentials/query/fragment/port/redirect; exact document identity and exact hosted callback.
OAUTH-03 DCR admits only the exact hosted callback and public none authentication, with shared fail-closed 5/minute and 20/hour limits, global 1000 cap and active-grant retention.
OAUTH-04 Code/S256/client/redirect/resource binding is exact; requests expire in ten minutes, codes in five, access in at most fifteen, family in thirty absolute days.
OAUTH-05 Consent requires live cookie session, exact Origin, browser/request/actor/session binding and single-use CSRF/decision; project selection is explicit, paginated and live-authorized.
OAUTH-06 No membership or board grant is created; current Owner inheritance and active non-Owner membership are preserved; ordinary tool authorization remains the parent-owned board boundary.

OAUTH-07 Code redemption and refresh issuance are atomic; separate-connection races cannot fork tokens; correctly bound reuse commits family revocation; wrong-client attempts cannot revoke victim grants.
OAUTH-08 Connection/access row locks precede existing project/board locks, conflict with revocation and deny subsequent operation/replay; stable connection ID survives refresh.
OAUTH-09 Raw codes/access/refresh/browser/CSRF credentials are never persisted in tables/logs/receipts/activity; strict response schemas prevent credential/internal-field leakage.
OAUTH-10 Own connection settings remain actor-owned and conceal new project metadata after membership loss; disconnect and OAuth revocation invalidate the family.
OAUTH-11 Bounded bodies, declared-Origin checks, standard OAuth errors, no-store responses, database-time expiry and failure rollback hold under the real mounted route module.

OAUTH-12 Additive PostgreSQL migration replays safely and matches embedded SQL; existing public PAT/session behavior is unchanged by this component. Integrated API/Worker/PAT regression remains mandatory before complete connector acceptance.

OAUTH-13 Consent and own connection summaries explicitly disclose offline persistence. Consent reports accessTokenLifetimeSeconds900, connectionLifetimeDays30 and refreshTokenIdleDays7 only when offlineAccess is true, otherwise null. Refresh issuance remains conditional on the approved offline_access scope.

OAUTH-14 Bounded scheduled retention preserves every code/refresh hash of retained families, keeps terminal connection identity for at least seven days after the conservative terminal/last-use anchor, deletes only orphan expired requests and protects live clients/pending authorization. SKIP LOCKED, hard100cap, real self-FK cascade, idempotence, scheduler rollback/continuation and immediate post-decision redaction pass isolated PostgreSQL tests.

OAUTH-15 Worker request pools remain alive until all reported image/MCP work truly settles, including rejected work. waitUntil retains asynchronous closure; without execution context closure is awaited. Mounted transport supplies the callback and its full integration remains part of final feature acceptance.

OAUTH-16 Exact OAuth/consent write paths enforce cancellable16KiB raw-byte reads and deadlines before generic buffering, including unfinished oversized/slow/already-aborted input. Cached JSON/form parsing preserves authority gates; actual downstream DB work is retained after HTTP timeout. Actual mounted regression evidence is mandatory.

TRANSPORT-01 Exact canonical OAuth-only MCP entry authenticates before SDK; cookies/PAT/query credentials and forged request identity cannot substitute; external OAuth remains invalid on REST/session/admin routes.

TRANSPORT-02 Exact discovery metadata, stateless JSON Streamable HTTP and five existing tools work; initialize, notification, list, call, errors, Accept/content-type/method/Origin/CORS and protocol bounds execute under Node and actual workerd.
TRANSPORT-03 Module-private Request identity retains principal and the same request pool; clones/headers cannot mint authority; no OAuth-to-PAT conversion or external arbitrary REST proxy exists.

TRANSPORT-04 Selected project and current Owner/Manager/Member/Viewer, membership and board grants remain authoritative for every operation and receipt retry; sibling/hidden board data is not exposed.

TRANSPORT-05 Create holds credential and live project/board/assignee authority through receipt/card/activity commit; stable connection ID binds semantic retries across refresh; changed input conflicts; concurrent revoke/create and grant removal cannot authorize later writes.

TRANSPORT-06 Protocol128KiB and JSON depth32 limits, no batches, connection120/minute/create30/minute fail-closed counters, deadlines and real-work cleanup are bounded. Declared/streamed oversize cancellation never blocks on uncooperative source cleanup; already-aborted and queued verification settle without later dispatch.
TRANSPORT-07 Unexpected errors and response projections never disclose raw credentials or SQL/provider diagnostics; receipts and safe mcp_oauth activity preserve privacy and one logical effect.

TRANSPORT-08 Existing full API/contracts/MCP/packed executable, typecheck/build, OpenAPI and embedded migration checks pass on the held target; no SQLite/mocked/native-helper claim substitutes for real PostgreSQL/Worker evidence.

HUI-01: Signed-out direct load to a real pending request. Continue with Google retains exact handle, synthetic provider roundtrip returns to that consent, name step if required retains URL; no landing-page detour or project disclosure while signed out. Bad/duplicate request input cannot enter a redirect.

HUI-02: Owner sees canonical name/origins, visible unverified warning, exact four permission labels, one explicit blank project choice and both decisions. Hidden sibling project/board names remain absent. Allow is disabled until choice; no All projects option.

HUI-03: Approve exactly one project. Capture only safe POST structural facts, one outcome and a callback matching exact scheme/host/path. No submitted redirect URI/scopes/client ID fields. Double click does not create two grants/codes. Callback is intercepted locally.
HUI-04: Deny with no project selection. POST omits projectId; callback error is access_denied, no code, and SQL count for own grants is unchanged. Reload/repeat cannot approve the consumed request.

HUI-05: Unknown, malformed, expired, missing browser binding and consumed requests show the generic unavailable state, no project/client leak, and disabled/absent allow. Expire synthetic row directly; do not wait10minutes.

HUI-06: Complete consent as Owner, Manager, Member and Viewer. The grant selects one existing project without inventing board authority. Viewer copy says actions remain limited by role; a grant cannot make a Viewer create cards. Personal Connections works for all four roles and an account with no projects.

HUI-07: Continuing-access and access-token-only requests show distinct truthful duration text on consent and Connections. For false, no7day/30day continuing-access claim; for true, all15minute/7day/30day policies appear.

HUI-08: More than100 currently accessible projects: Load more preserves current explicit selection, appends distinct choices, honors nextCursor and submits newest CSRF. Loading next page does not automatically choose another project or reset permissions.

HUI-09: Switch actor/session after consent GET. Old project/client details are removed and the decision fails closed; membership removal between view and allow fails. Reload obtains canonical state rather than retrying the old CSRF or replacing project choice silently.

HUI-10: Connections shows safe app/project/scopes/date/expiry and “Not recorded” for null last use; no success/last-use claim inferred from approval. Disconnect confirmation names the app/project; Escape preserves grant and returns focus, confirm sends one DELETE204 and removes row. Direct same-user repeated DELETE stays204; outsider ID remains non-disclosing.

HUI-11: Lost decision response, OAuth400/401/403/404/409/429/503 and non-JSON faults show local copy and safe recovery. No raw SQL/stack/provider message, URL/code/secret or exception text. Honor Retry-After; no auto-post on GET/reload. Failed POST state is unknown, not falsely approved/denied.

HUI-12: Malicious client name is inert text, no remote logo/script fetch. Record console warnings/errors, page errors, unexpected API failures, external origins and DOM diagnostic/credential-pattern scan; successful cases require zero unexpected events. Expected security refusals are recorded by status/path only.

HUI-13: Keyboard-only choice/allow/deny/navigation/disconnect, visible focus and alert/status names; dialog Escape/focus restore;320px/200% zoom and long names fit without clipped action controls. Capture consent and Connections screenshots only before callback URLs contain codes.

HUI-14: Built static export through actual Pages Functions: direct `/connect` load/refresh works; all exact well-known metadata aliases proxy with protocol JSON and no sign-in redirect; existing `/api/*` no-store/cookies survive. Next dev evidence does not close this case.

HUI-15: Current unchanged stdio/PAT/browser flows, actual mounted OAuth→MCP tool calls and post-disconnect rejection pass final integration suites. The draft UI composition is not proof of private dispatcher or Worker behavior.
